temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He invites Gary to a weekend retreat, but Gary declines because there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dedicated and hardworking, but he has not yet fully accepted that Gary's habits may be seriously harming his health.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: noticing Gary's excessive work and self-neglect makes Ethan believe Gary is at risk; Gary's refusal confirms that the hospital workload is intense and that Gary is resistant to stepping away.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is seriously overworked and needs help, but he feels trapped by his obligations at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, worried, and somewhat disappointed by Gary's refusal.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find relief or support despite his resistance, perhaps by persisting gently or finding another way to intervene.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes that Gary is restless and avoids discussions about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked and hopes the retreat setting will help Gary relax and open up.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's restlessness and avoidance suggest his overwork is not only a professional scheduling issue; something deeper or more personal is troubling him.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is hiding or struggling with an underlying problem beyond ordinary hospital duties.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, suspicious, and worried for Gary.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To confront Gary gently and offer nonjudgmental support so Gary might confide in him.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After Ethan confronts him, Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects there is more behind Gary's overwork and wants Gary to trust him with the truth.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Ethan now understands the specific pressures and personal challenges causing Gary's behavior.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary's overwork is a response to significant professional and personal stress, and Gary is willing to accept help.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better balance, starting with prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan checks in regularly. Gary reports progress, says he is less overwhelmed, and mentions having had time for a movie.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is working toward better balance but still faces challenges and needs encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's reports and efforts show that meaningful improvement is actually happening.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is making real progress toward a healthier work-life balance and can continue improving with support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, encouraging Gary, and offering support whenever needed.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Ethan sees that Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and can manage on his own. Gary thanks Ethan for his support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has improved but may still need some ongoing support or reassurance.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's successful adjustment shows that he is now capable of managing independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary no longer needs active intervention; Ethan can step back while remaining available if needed.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Satisfied, happy, and proud for Gary.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back and let Gary manage independently, while making clear he is always available if Gary needs him.
